text: Leaving his family at home. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom set out with his servant. <break time="0.8s" /> Taking tea, wine, and other presents. <break time="0.8s" /> For the Bashkirs. <break time="0.8s" /> The Bashkirs lived in tents. <break time="0.8s" /> On the wide steppe. <break time="0.8s" /> Where they kept horses and drank mares milk. <break time="0.8s" /> They did not plow the land at all. <break time="0.8s" /> And they spent the summer. <break time="0.8s" /> Drinking tea, eating mutton. <break time="0.8s" /> And playing music. <break time="0.8s" /> Pleased with Pahoms gifts. <break time="0.8s" /> They told him through an interpreter. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could choose any land he liked. <break time="0.8s" /> Then their chief arrived. <break time="0.8s" /> In a fox fur cap. <break time="0.8s" /> And Pahom asked him. <break time="0.8s" /> What price he wanted for the land. <break time="0.8s" /> Our price is always the same. <break time="0.8s" /> One thousand rubles a day. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the chief. <break time="0.8s" /> And Pahom did not understand. <break time="0.8s" /> The chief explained that Pahom could have all the land. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could walk around in one day. <break time="0.8s" /> But if you do not return. <break time="0.8s" /> To the starting place before sunset. <break time="0.8s" /> Your money is lost. <break time="0.8s" /> He warned. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom was so excited. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could not sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking of the huge piece of land. <break time="0.8s" /> He would mark out. <break time="0.8s" /> Just before dawn. <break time="0.8s" /> He dozed off. <break time="0.8s" /> And dreamed of the Devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Laughing beside a dead man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was Pahom himself.
